question: A right-angled triangle ABC has legs AB=6 cm and BC=8 cm. An altitude BD is drawn from the vertex B to the hypotenuse AC. What is the length of the altitude BD?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a right-angled triangle, the altitude drawn to the hypotenuse is given by the direct formula: **Altitude = (Perpendicular × Base) ÷ Hypotenuse**.

Hypotenuse AC = √(6² + 8²) = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10 cm.

Altitude BD = (AB × BC) ÷ AC = (6 × 8) ÷ 10 = 4.8 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.8 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Legs of right-angled triangle AB = 6 cm and BC = 8 cm.

 
 
• 
 
 A B C D 6 cm 8 cm h = ? 
• 
• 
• 10 cm 

**Formula Used:**

Area of a triangle = 1/2 × Base × Height

Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base²

**Calculations:**

⇒ By Pythagoras theorem, AC² = AB² + BC²

⇒ AC = √(6² + 8²) = √(36 + 64) = √100 = 10 cm

⇒ Area of ∆ABC using legs as base and height = 1/2 × AB × BC

⇒ Area = 1/2 × 6 × 8 = 24 cm²

⇒ We can also express Area of ∆ABC using the hypotenuse as the base: Area = 1/2 × AC × BD

⇒ 24 = 1/2 × 10 × BD

⇒ 24 = 5 × BD

⇒ BD = 24 ÷ 5 = 4.8 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 4.8 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Altitude to Hypotenuse Area Rule

The product of the legs of a right triangle is always equal to the product of the hypotenuse and the altitude drawn to it (Leg₁ × Leg₂ = Hypotenuse × Altitude).

Similar Triangles Theorem

Drawing an altitude to the hypotenuse of a right triangle divides it into two smaller triangles that are mathematically similar to each other and to the original parent triangle.

Geometric Mean Theorem

The altitude drawn to the hypotenuse acts as the geometric mean of the lengths of the two smaller segments it divides the hypotenuse into: h² = Segment₁ × Segment₂.
